about.heading: About me
about.intro: I'm a software developer in Aksaray, Turkey. I work across the full stack — C#, ASP.NET Core and SQL Server on the server, Next.js and TypeScript in the browser — and I came to it through a structured programming track, then through building systems.
learning: I studied through ProgrammingAdvices, a structured track covering the areas in sequence: programming fundamentals and problem solving, C++, object-oriented programming, data structures, databases and SQL Server, then C# and ASP.NET Core and full-stack development.
since: Since then the work has been projects. One of them is an AI workspace — ASP.NET Core in four layers, a Python retrieval service, PostgreSQL and Qdrant, and a language model running locally — 598 files and 74 merged pull requests, feature-complete and waiting on deployment. Another is a three-tier desktop system that runs a restaurant’s purchasing and inventory on SQL Server, where every database call goes through a stored procedure.
about.looking: Freelance projects, remote roles, or local work. I live in Aksaray and I am open to positions in Ankara.

projects.heading: Projects
projects.intro: Two systems, both built end to end. The first is an AI workspace whose retrieval pipeline runs entirely on its own hardware; the second is a desktop application that handles a restaurant's purchasing and inventory on SQL Server.

aiWorkspace.name: AI Autonomous Workspace
aiWorkspace.summary: Documents pile up faster than anyone reads them. This workspace ingests them, indexes what is inside, and answers questions with the source attached.
aiWorkspace.highlight: A 35-page PDF, from upload to searchable in 32.6 seconds.
aiWorkspace.problem: Documents pile up faster than anyone reads them. This workspace ingests them, indexes what is inside, and answers questions about them with the source page attached.
aiWorkspace.result: Measured on a running system rather than estimated: a 35-page PDF goes from upload to searchable in 32.6 seconds, and every answer returns with the page it was drawn from.
architecture: ASP.NET Core in four layers — Domain, Application, Infrastructure and Api — with a Python FastAPI service doing the retrieval, PostgreSQL and Qdrant in Docker, and the language model running locally. No third-party AI provider: extraction, embeddings, retrieval and generation all run on the project's own hardware.
aiWorkspace.scale: 598 files · 189 C# · 80 Python · 41 TypeScript · 85 test files · 74 merged pull requests
aiWorkspace.scope: Feature-complete through its ninth sprint. The tenth is release preparation, so the system is built and verified but not yet deployed.

restaurant.name: Restaurant Management
restaurant.summary: Purchasing and inventory for a restaurant, built as a Windows desktop application with an Arabic, right-to-left interface.
restaurant.highlight: 9 forms, 10 tables, 37 stored procedures — and no inline SQL anywhere.
restaurant.problem: Purchasing and inventory for a restaurant, built as a Windows desktop application.
architecture: Three tiers — forms, business logic, data access — with every database call going through a stored procedure and none through inline SQL.
restaurant.scale: 9 forms · 10 tables · 37 stored procedures · RDLC reports
restaurant.notable: The interface is Arabic and right-to-left throughout, which is where I first learned how much of a layout is direction-dependent.
